newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN OPPOSITION BACKS KWV AGAINST MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN OPPOSITION BACKS KWV AGAINST MINISTER.

text.p: South Africa's oppposition National Party accused Agriculture Minister Derek Hanekom of attempting communist-style nationalisation on Thursday after he forced the postponement of the KWV wine co-operative's bid to become a private company.
Hanekom won court approval this week to intervene in the KWV plan to restructure by the end of the month, effectively postponing the process until at least August 18.

The minister said he wanted to study if the plan would transfer state assets into private hands, if it would give KWV an unfair advantage in the market, and if it would lead to a regulatory vacuum in the wine and spirits industry.
KWV is currently stautory regulator of the industry.

National Party agriculture spokesman Manie Schoeman said in a speech in parliament that Hanekom's actions in the KWV case exemplified his "total onslaught on the commercial agricultural sector and its institutions".
"It would seem that once again he is acting contrary to government policy through subtly supporting and implementing a communist-inspired policy of nationalisation of private assets," Schoeman said.
He said KWV wanted to convert to a private company so it could compete more effectively in international markets. KWV is active in about 50 countries.
"The minister is determined to nationalise private assets under the pretext of public interest -- assets which have been built up by KWV members and belongs in total to them," Schoeman said.
